# Project Context: OrderApp (ASP.NET Core MVC & Web API)
This repository contains a lightweight order management system built using ASP.NET Core MVC for presentation and Web API controllers for data manipulation.

## Core Domain Model
The application operates on a single core entity: `Order`.
- `Id` (int): Unique identifier generated by the backend.
- `Title` (string): Required, min length 3 characters, max length 50 characters.
- `Description` (string, nullable): Optional details about the order.
- `Price` (decimal): Numeric value, allowed range from 1 to 10000.
- `Quantity` (int): Numeric value, allowed range from 1 to 100.
- `TotalPrice` (decimal): Read-only calculated property via the formula `Price * Quantity`.

## Coding Conventions & Guidelines

### Backend (C# / .NET)
- Always use the explicit `[ApiController]` and `[Route("api/[controller]")]` attributes on all API controllers.
- Data persistence must utilize the static In-Memory collection `_orders` located inside `OrdersController`. Do not add database contexts or repositories unless explicitly instructed.
- All incoming requests in POST or PUT methods must strictly evaluate `ModelState.IsValid`. Return `BadRequest(ModelState)` if validation fails.
- The `TotalPrice` property must never be written to or accepted via HTTP request bodies. Keep it as an automated runtime property: `public decimal TotalPrice => Price * Quantity;`.
- Handle missing entities via proper HTTP response status codes: return `NotFound(new { message = "..." })` if an entity by ID does not exist.

### Frontend (HTML / JavaScript / Razor)
- Form rendering must happen within Razor Views located in the `Views/Home/` directory.
- Input validation must be implemented natively on the client-side using standard HTML5 validation attributes: `required`, `minlength="3"`, `maxlength="50"`, `min="1"`, `max="10000"`.
- Calculate `TotalPrice` asynchronously on the client-side using JavaScript event listeners (`input`) immediately when the `Price` or `Quantity` fields change.
- All custom scripts within Razor Views (`.cshtml` files) must be wrapped inside the `@section Scripts { ... }` block to ensure correct loading sequence after shared layout dependencies.
- Use native `fetch` API for all AJAX network operations targeting the API backend.

### Response Constraints
- Do not add code comments, annotations, or instructional inline text blocks within the generated source code.
- Write clean, production-ready, self-documenting code following standard C# PascalCase naming conventions for properties and methods.
